t01.style: Cinematic still from a 2000s American prescription-drug television commercial, black and white, desaturated, melancholy, soft diffused lighting, gentle depth of field, shot on 35mm film, photorealistic. The same woman appears: early 30s, box braids, olive blazer over a white t-shirt.
t01.content: She sits in a dark home office lit only by a laptop screen, dozens of tiny tab shapes glowing along the top of the screen, her face weary.

t02.content: Extreme close-up of her tired eyes with the laptop light reflecting in them, a faint whirring fan sound implied by dust drifting past the vent.

t03.content: She hugs the open laptop protectively against her chest and looks directly at the camera, calm and completely serious.

t04.content: Product shot from a television pharmaceutical commercial: an amber prescription pill bottle with a clean white label; the label reads TABZOLAM in large letters, and beneath it in smaller letters BROWSOLAM and EXTENDED RELEASE TABLETS 25 mg; the bottle stands on a seamless soft white studio background, bathed in warm golden light, gentle glow, photorealistic.

t05.content: Close on one finger hovering over the keyboard, then pressing a single key with ceremony; her face floods with relief; warm color blooming into the scene.

t08.content: A quiet home office: closed laptop, a thriving plant, morning light; she sits with tea, listening to the silence with wonder.

t09.content: Minimal end card for a television pharmaceutical commercial: flat solid cream background, the word TABZOLAM in large elegant dark serif capital letters centered, beneath it in smaller letters the tagline: You were never going to read them. A small amber pill bottle sits below the text. Clean flat studio typography, no gradients. The small bottle's label shows only the word TABZOLAM in tiny letters and no other text.
